name: Formation of the Lombard League
summary: Sixteen northern Italian communes, led by Milan and supported by Pope Alexander III, form the Lombard League at Pontida in April 1167 to resist Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa's efforts to reassert direct imperial control over Italian cities. Frederick had razed Milan in 1162; the League rebuilds it and constructs a new fortress city, Alessandria, specifically to block imperial invasion routes. The allied cities field professional communal militias trained to fight on foot.

_quarry.structural_significance: Demonstrates that urban communes can defeat feudal emperors when organized collectively; the League's victory at Legnano (1176) forces Frederick to recognize communal self-governance in the Peace of Constance (1183); establishes the legal precedent for Italian city autonomy that shapes the Renaissance era; the Lombard League is revived in the 13th century against Frederick II
